invest: A shareholder is a co-owner of the company: they can receive dividends and gain from its growth in value, but can also lose.
A debt security: you lend money at interest
By buying a bond you lend money to the state or a company. In return you get coupons and the face value back on time.
Part of the profit the company pays to shareholders
Companies are not obliged to pay dividends: the amount depends on profit and the shareholders' decision.
Putting all money into one share
"Don't put all your eggs in one basket": a fall in one asset is partly offset by the others.
How are return and risk usually related?
The higher the possible return, the higher the risk
You pay for return with risk.
A promise of high return without risk is the main sign of fraud.
An intermediary for buying securities on an exchange
You go to the exchange through them.
A private investor cannot trade on an exchange directly: a brokerage account is needed. Check the broker's license.
A set of assets you can buy a share of with one security
A fund gives diversification even for a small amount. It charges a management fee, which is worth comparing.
The period for which you invest money
How long you are ready to wait.
The longer the horizon, the more risk you can afford: short-term drawdowns have time to recover.
Does the exchange guarantee income on shares?
No, shares can also fall in price
Yes, if you buy a lot
Unlike deposits, investments are not insured by the state: you can lose part of the money.
A measure of price changes of a group of large stocks
An index shows how the prices of selected stocks change on average. It is used to judge the market and compare your own results.
A regular interest payment to the bondholder
Coupons are paid quarterly, semi-annually or annually. For fixed-coupon bonds the amount is known in advance.
What happens to the price of already issued bonds when interest rates in the economy rise?
New ones come out with a higher coupon.
New bonds come out with a higher coupon, and old low-coupon ones become less attractive and cheaper.
Why is putting everything into one "promising" startup risky?
No diversification: you can lose everything
Most startups do not survive. Putting all money into one project removes the protection that diversification gives.
Buying the stock that has grown most
Returning asset shares to target proportions
Bring the shares back to the plan.
For example, the target is 60% stocks and 40% bonds. Stocks grew to 70%, so part of them is sold and bonds are bought.
What is an IIA, an individual investment account (in Russia)?
An individual investment account with tax benefits
An account with a tax benefit.
An IIA gives tax benefits if conditions are met: holding period and limits. The rules have changed, so check the current terms.
What is a fund management fee?
An annual percentage of your assets in the fund
1–2% a year seems small, but over 20 years it eats a noticeable part of the income. Low fees are an important selection criterion.
Regularly buying assets for the same amount regardless of price is…
When prices are low you buy more securities, when high, fewer. This reduces the risk of a bad entry moment.
Trading with money borrowed from the broker
Leverage magnifies both profits and losses. If prices fall, the broker can force-sell the securities. It is not for beginners.
Why should you not invest the money from your safety cushion?
The broker will not accept it
When you need it, the assets may be in a drawdown
The money may be needed suddenly.
The cushion is needed exactly at a bad moment, and the market often falls at such moments too. Selling in a drawdown means locking in a loss.
A share rose 50% and then fell 50%. The result?
The price returned to the original
100 → 150 → 75. A 50% fall "eats" more than a 50% rise added.
How quickly it can be sold without losing value
An on-demand deposit is very liquid, an apartment is not: it can be sold quickly only at a discount.
A fall in value from the previous peak
How far it fell from the peak.
Drawdowns are a normal part of investing. It is important to know in advance which one you can live through without selling everything in panic.
The rule of 72: money doubles in about 72 ÷ rate years. At 8% a year that is:
72 / 8 = 9 years. The rule works for compound interest and quickly estimates the doubling time.
What is a financial pyramid scheme?
A scheme where old members are paid with new members' money
Where do the payouts come from?
A pyramid collapses when the inflow of new money ends. Signs: guaranteed high income, bonuses for recruits, an unclear business.
Nominal return 12%, inflation 9%. The real return is approximately:
More precisely: 1.12 / 1.09 − 1 ≈ 2.75%. Real return shows how much purchasing power has grown.
What does the P/E ratio show?
The share price relative to earnings per share
P/E shows how many years it would take the company to "pay back" its price at current earnings. A high P/E means growth expectations or overvaluation.
Why does a broad index fund often beat active managers over a long horizon?
Most active funds fail to consistently beat the market over 10–15 years after fees.
You invested 100,000 ₽ at 10% a year with reinvestment. In 20 years there will be about:
1.1^20 ≈ 6.73. Over 20 years compound interest multiplies capital almost 7 times, while simple interest would give only 300,000 ₽.
Why consider the correlation of assets in a portfolio?
It is the speed of selling an asset
Weakly related assets together reduce overall risk
Do they fall at the same time?
If assets do not fall in sync, the drawdown of one is partly offset by another. That is why portfolios hold different asset classes.
A bond with a 1,000 ₽ face value was bought for 950 ₽, the coupon is 80 ₽ a year, maturity in a year. The yield to maturity is about:
Coupon plus the difference to face value.
Income = 80 ₽ coupon + 50 ₽ difference (950 → 1,000) = 130 ₽. 130 / 950 ≈ 13.7% before taxes and fees.
tax: A mandatory payment to the state
A fine for a late loan payment
Taxes fund schools, hospitals, roads and other public goods. Paying them is mandatory by law.
What is personal income tax, NDFL (in Russia)?
It is usually withheld from salary by the employer. The base rate is 13%, with higher rates for large incomes.
Who usually pays the income tax on your salary?
The employer withholds and pays it for you
The employer is a tax agent. That is why the salary arrives on your card already net of tax.
A way to get back part of the tax paid
Deductions are available, for example, for buying housing, medical treatment, education, investments. You need to claim them yourself or through your employer.
A tax on house and garden
Value added tax included in the price of goods
It is already in the price.
All buyers pay VAT: it is simply "hidden" in the price of goods and services.
How much do the self-employed (NPD, in Russia) pay on income from individuals?
Professional income tax: 4% on payments from individuals and 6% from companies and sole proprietors. There is an annual income limit.
What happens if you do not pay taxes on time?
Penalties accrue, there may be a fine and forced collection
The debt to the state grows.
Penalties accrue for each day of delay, and the debt can be collected from your accounts. It is easier to pay on time.
Where is it convenient to check your taxes and file a return (in Russia)?
The tax office's official online service.
The personal account shows assessed taxes, deductions and the status of returns.
Is a cash gift from a close relative subject to income tax (in Russia)?
Gifts from close relatives, parents, children, spouses, siblings, grandparents, are not subject to income tax.
A person staying in the country 183 days or more a year
Days in the country are counted.
Tax rates and the right to deductions depend on residency. Non-residents usually pay more.
The maximum cost of housing for the property purchase deduction (in Russia):
You can get back 13% of it.
From 2 million ₽ you can get back up to 260,000 ₽. There is a separate deduction for mortgage interest on up to 3 million ₽.
Can you get a deduction for medical treatment or education (in Russia)?
Yes, it is a social deduction within an annual limit
The total limit of social deductions is now 150,000 ₽ a year, so you can get back up to 19,500 ₽. Expensive treatment has no limit.
For how many past years can you claim a tax deduction (in Russia)?
A deduction can be claimed for the three previous years, so it is fine if you did not apply on time.
What do you need to get a tax deduction?
Just file an application without documents
Have income taxed with income tax and supporting documents
A deduction returns tax already paid. No tax, nothing to return (except for certain categories).
How is deposit interest taxed (in Russia)?
Income tax is paid only on income above a tax-free threshold
It is not taxed at all
The bank pays the tax from its own money
The tax-free threshold is calculated from the key rate and 1 million ₽. The tax office calculates the tax on the excess and sends a notice.
You sold your only home, which you owned for 7 years. Do you have to pay income tax (in Russia)?
No, the ownership period exceeds the minimum
Only if sold for more than 1 million
For one's only home the minimum ownership period is 3 years, in other cases usually 5 years.
What is the standard child deduction (in Russia)?
A monthly reduction of a parent's taxable income
The employer withholds less income tax, and take-home pay is a bit higher. The deduction applies up to a certain income level.
What deduction is due for buying an apartment for 3 million ₽ without a mortgage (in Russia)?
The cost limit is 2 million ₽, 13% of it is 260,000 ₽. The deduction can be received over several years until the full amount is reached.
How should a self-employed person record income (in Russia)?
Issue a receipt in the "My Tax" app for each payment
Sign a contract with the tax office
The tax is calculated automatically from the receipts issued, and it must be paid by the 28th of the following month.
What is a progressive tax scale?
The rate is the same for everyone
The rate decreases for the rich
In Russia since 2025 income tax has been progressive: 13% on income up to 2.4 million ₽ a year, beyond that rates rise in steps.
The deadline for individuals to pay property and vehicle taxes (in Russia):
By December 1 of the following year
Closer to the end of the year.
The tax office sends a notice, and it must be paid by December 1 of the following year, conveniently via the personal account or a bank.
You rent out an apartment. Do you have to pay tax (in Russia)?
No, if the apartment is your own
Only if the tenant is a foreigner
Only when renting out for more than 5 years
You can pay income tax with a return or register as self-employed and pay 4% on payments from individuals.
Mortgage interest paid totaled 1 million ₽. How much income tax can be returned (in Russia)?
The interest deduction applies to up to 3 million ₽. From 1 million ₽ of interest, 13% = 130,000 ₽ is returned.
What is the 3-NDFL tax return for (in Russia)?
To report income without withheld tax or claim a deduction
To get a passport for travel abroad
An income return is filed by April 30, and the tax on it is paid by July 15. For claiming a deduction this deadline is not mandatory.
Why is it important to keep the minimum holding period on an IIA with a tax deduction?
Otherwise the broker charges a 50% fine
If closed early, the deduction received must be returned
A benefit in exchange for time.
IIA tax benefits are given if the period is kept. Close the account early and the state will demand the deduction back.
How does the income tax rate on salary differ for a non-resident (in Russia)?
For most non-resident income the rate is 30%, and deductions are not available. There are exceptions for certain categories.
A lottery win of 300,000 ₽. What is the tax (in Russia)?
Winnings are subject to income tax. The first 4,000 ₽ a year are tax-free, the rest is taxed at the resident rate.
A side job of 30,000 ₽ a month from individuals. What is better: NPD or ordinary income tax (in Russia)?
1,200 ₽ versus 3,900 ₽ a month. Also, when registering as self-employed you get a 10,000 ₽ deduction that lowers the rate at the start.
What is the fastest way to find out about tax debt (in Russia)?
Wait for a letter from collectors
Check the taxpayer's personal account or Gosuslugi
The debt is visible in the personal account and on Gosuslugi. You can pay it right there without waiting for penalties.
What is the maximum you can get back for all social deductions in a year with a 150,000 ₽ limit?
13% × 150,000 = 19,500 ₽. The limit is shared for treatment, education, sports and a number of other expenses.
fraud: A "bank employee" calls and asks for the code from an SMS. What should you do?
Hang up and call the bank back on the number on your card
The bank never asks for such codes.
The SMS code is the key to your money. A real bank never asks for it. Call back only on the official number.
Can a real bank ask for the CVC code by phone?
The bank does not need the CVC for service. Only scammers ask for it.
You got an SMS: "Your card is blocked, call back at…". What should you do?
Reply to the SMS with a code
Do not call the number from the SMS, check in the bank app instead
The number in the SMS may belong to someone else.
Check your card's status in the official app or by the number on the back of the card.
Fake websites and emails to steal data
Check the website address, do not follow links from emails and SMS, enter card details only on familiar sites.
A stranger promises a "guaranteed income of 30% a month". This is most likely…
Nobody can guarantee such a return. It is a classic sign of a pyramid or a scam.
A friend writes in a messenger: "Urgently lend me 10,000, I'll explain later". What should you do?
Call the friend by voice and check
Forward the message to the bank
Accounts are often hacked and requests are sent to contacts. A voice call will clear doubts in a minute.
What is a "safe account" you are asked to transfer money to?
A protected account at the central bank
A deposit with a higher rate
A scammers' invention, such accounts do not exist
Neither a bank, nor the police, nor the central bank asks you to transfer money to "safe accounts". It is always a scam.
Can you tell the cashier your PIN if the terminal is not working?
Yes, if the cashier is polite
No, you always enter the PIN yourself
The PIN is never told to anyone: not a cashier, not a bank employee, not a relative.
You won a prize, but they ask you to pay for "delivery" or "tax". This is…
A real prize does not require prepayment.
You pay tax on a prize yourself to the tax office, not to the organizers. A request to pay in advance is a sign of a scam.
How do you protect a banking app account?
A strong password, two-factor protection and updates
Write the password in your phone notes
A unique password, a second factor and fresh system updates close most hacking methods.
You expected the site mybank.ru, but "mybank.ru.secure-login.top" opened. What is wrong?
It is a fake domain, the real address is different
Look at the end of the address.
The real domain is the last part of the address before the first "/": here it is secure-login.top. Type the bank's address manually or use a bookmark.
A call "from the police": a relative was in an accident and money is needed to "settle the matter". What should you do?
Hang up and call the relative yourself
Quickly hand money to a courier
Scammers press on fear and urgency. Call the relative directly: in most cases they are fine.
What is the danger of handing over your card or account to third parties for a reward?
Stolen money will be run through your account, and you will be held responsible
You will be made a link in the chain.
"Easy money" from handing over a card leads to blocked accounts and criminal liability.
A seller on a classifieds site asks you to pay via his "safe deal" link. What is suspicious?
The link may lead to a fake payment page
A low price is always honest
The link is not from the platform.
Use a safe deal only inside the platform's official app and do not move to messengers.
How do you recognize a pyramid scheme?
High income promised, bonuses for recruits, an unclear business
An office in the city center
If it is unclear how they earn, but high income is guaranteed, it is a pyramid.
You are offered to "get money back for poor-quality goods" but first pay a "duty". What is it?
Scammers buy databases of victims and deceive them again, promising to return what was lost.
Why is it dangerous to install apps at the request of a "security service"?
The apps will take up memory
It may be a remote phone control program
Through remote access programs scammers see the screen and codes and can carry out transactions themselves.
A QR code on a parking machine leads to a payment site. What should you check?
Whether a fake code is stuck over the real one
The parking price in a neighboring city
A sticker is easy to swap.
Scammers stick their QR codes over real ones. Check the site address and pay through the official app.
Check the lender in the official register. Illegal lenders use threats and enslaving terms.
What is the safest way to pay online?
With a separate card with a small balance and payment confirmation
With your main card holding all savings
By transfer to a stranger by number
By sending the seller a photo of your card
Even if data leaks, there will be little money on a separate card, and payment confirmation will stop unauthorized charges.
"Your Gosuslugi account has been hacked, tell us the code to cancel". The right reaction:
Do not tell the code, it will let them into your account
Forward the code to a friend
Tell the code but ask them to confirm their identity
They need the code, not you.
This very code will let scammers into your account. Hang up and check the login yourself.
A sign of a fake online store:
Card payment via a payment service
Prices far below market and payment only by transfer to a card
Incredible discounts and payment by transfer to an individual's card are classic signs of a fly-by-night site.
Manipulating people so they hand over data or money themselves
Hacking a person, not a computer.
Scammers press with urgency, fear or gain. The best protection is a pause and a check through official channels.
You received a confirmation code although you did nothing. What does it mean?
The bank is checking the connection
A system error, you can ignore it
Someone is trying to log into your account or make a transaction
Do not share the code with anyone, change your password and check active sessions.
You transferred money to scammers. What should you do first?
Immediately tell the bank and file a police report
The sooner the bank knows, the greater the chance to stop the transaction. Save the messages and numbers.
Why can banks delay suspicious transfers?
To give the client time to reconsider and protect them from scammers
Banks can suspend transactions that look fraudulent and contact the client before the money leaves.
Why are calls with a faked voice (deepfakes) dangerous?
A familiar person's voice or video can be faked
A recognizable voice is no guarantee.
Agree on a code word with your family and always double-check requests for money through another channel.
An investment platform shows huge "profit", but asks you to pay a "tax" upfront to withdraw. This is…
A classic scheme: the money will not be returned
Pay for the right to take your own?
The numbers on the screen are decoration. After the "tax" they will ask for "insurance", then a "fee", and there will be no withdrawal.
What is a self-ban on loans (in Russia)?
A ban on issuing loans to you that you set yourself
The self-ban is set via Gosuslugi. It prevents taking a loan in your name without your knowledge, and it can be lifted at any time.
You are offered a job: receive money on your card and pass it on for a percentage. What does this threaten?
Nothing, it is a side job
Liability for taking part in moving stolen money
This is how scammers move stolen funds. The cardholder becomes an accomplice and risks a criminal case.
